No industry-sponsored nasal orexin, NPY, cannabinoid, zuranolone/neurosteroid, apomorphine (beyond Oncotelic licensing, undated) or GLP-1 nose-to-brain CNS program in clinic was found. pain_emergency: WebSearch budget (shared, 200/turn) ran out mid-task, so the last few checks (TNX-1900 program status, Sichuan Purity dexmedetomidine details, FDA acceptance of the IZIPRY resubmission) were not searched; these rely on earlier results. (1) Trudhesa owner: the Feb 2024 court approved the sale of Impel's assets to stalking-horse bidder JN Bidco LLC, and one tracker says the buyer was 'undisclosed'. trudhesa.com still reads (c) 2026 Impel Pharmaceuticals. The parent behind JN Bidco is UNVERIFIED. (2) CT001 US pathway: shipment through STAQ Pharma, which may be a 503B outsourcing facility (UNVERIFIED); it is not confirmed as an FDA-approved NDA. EU: negative CHMP PUMA opinion in July 2026 (exact day UNVERIFIED), and Proveca plans a re-examination. Lane 'market' is debatable. (3) Atzumi: approved Apr 2025, but the US commercial launch date is not confirmed; as of May 2026 SNBL was still building the team. NCT04940390 (SUMMIT) outcome not re-verified. (4) Zavzpret: Asian Ph3 NCT05989048 (China/Korea/Taiwan) gave 2-h pain freedom of 23.2% vs 14.1% (p<0.0001) per CT.gov results. The China NDA was accepted Dec 2025 and approval is not yet found. No Korea MFDS filing was found, and the Korea filing status is UNVERIFIED (relevant to KR audience). No evidence of discontinuation. (5) neffy: no Korea partner found. China approval (Dec 2025, Pediatrix) and Japan approval (Sep 2025) appear in search summaries. The Japan launch date of 12 Feb comes from a Jiho snippet (year inferred 2026). ARS-2 in the CSU trial is assumed to be the neffy formulation. (6) Bryn Utuly: last public item is Jun 2025, and the Q3 2025 PK/PD readout and NDA status are UNVERIFIED. (7) Opvee strength (2.7 mg) and device makers for Narcan/neffy/Zavzpret (commonly Aptar UDS) were not re-verified this session, so they are marked accordingly. (8) Excluded: Aspeya ASY202 DHE is an ORAL INHALATION powder (NCT07226362, NCT07646613), not nasal. Purdue nalmefene autoinjector is IM. Tosymra (Tonix) has no notable 2025-26 news. RiVive has no 2025-26 news (kept for OTC landscape). Nasus FMXIN001 naloxone powder shows no activity since 2022. (9) Lane choices: Nasus FMXIN002 set to p2 although the top trial is labeled Phase 2/3. OX640 set to early (IND just accepted, pivotal PK not started). Dexmedetomidine nasal products and Kovanaze are tagged area 'Other' (procedural sedation/dental anesthesia).
vaccines: Search budget for this run was exhausted near the end, so some details are flagged UNVERIFIED rather than checked. Biggest uncertainties: (1) Current real-world status of the approved nasal COVID vaccines (iNCOVACC, Pneucolin, Sputnik nasal): no 2025-26 primary sources were found; they are kept as 'market' based on the original authorizations, and current supply is UNVERIFIED. (2) CVXGA Phase 2b: the registry shows COMPLETED with only 432 enrolled (the plan was ~10,000), which suggests the BARDA efficacy study was cut back; no topline results found. (3) CastleVax: the BARDA Phase 2b efficacy award was 'paused, may be terminated' per the Absolutely Maybe tracker, not confirmed by the company. (4) Codagenix CoviLiv: the WHO Solidarity Phase 3 outcome and registry ID are unknown; the end of the BARDA award comes from GHTC's reading of spending data. I put it in 'stopped', which is a judgment call. (5) BPZE1 is lane p2 because Phase 3 start is not confirmed; the hVIVO contract date (22 Apr 2026) comes from search snippets because the RNS page failed to load. (6) Fluenz self-administration: the EMA assessment report (25 Jun 2026 per search snippet) was not readable, so the EC decision is UNVERIFIED. (7) BCHT news date 2025-08-03 is the reported Changchun rollout date; the approval was 'Aug 2025' per the company disclosure, exact day unknown. (8) Meissa lastMove 2023-08 is approximate; the Fierce article date was not confirmed. (9) The CONTAIN azelastine trial registry ID was not found on CT.gov; NCT06008860 is a separate UChicago Astepro study. (10) Nasodine PVP-I concentration and US launch date are not confirmed. SaNOtize also reportedly rebranded Enovid as 'NoWonder' via BuyEnov in the US (Oct 2025, marketed for nasal hygiene), but I did not open a primary URL for this. Excluded or not carded: Vaxart (oral), CD388 (injectable), Convidecia (inhaled), Aerovax (aerosol). No intranasal mpox vaccine in clinical trials was found. BLB301 could not be identified. Lumen LMN-1001 (intranasal, Phase 1 NCT07852208 not yet recruiting, start Nov 2026, US Army-funded; molecule identity UNVERIFIED), CyanVac intranasal mumps vaccines CVM150/CVM26 (Phase 1 NCT06967181, n=60), Rokote Laboratories (Finland) nasal COVID vector second Phase 1 NCT07416539 (n=20, fully recruited), LovalTech/Univ. Tours LVT-001 Phase 1/2 vs Comirnaty (NCT06821126, ANRS, n=238; phase 2 funding uncertain), and TANCoV (Tanzania) are candidates for extra cards. Also not carded: older approved nasal LAIVs (Russia Microgen, India Serum Institute Nasovac-S) and Iran's Razi Cov Pars (intranasal booster component).
metabolic_ent: Search budget for the session ran out partway through, so some items could not be cross-checked. (1) ETRIPAMIL (high confidence): FDA approved 12 Dec 2025 after a CRL and resubmission (new PDUFA 13 Dec 2025). Available at US retail pharmacies late Jan 2026, promoted from mid-Feb 2026. Q2 2026 net product revenue was $0.56M (H1 $0.80M). China NMPA approved it 3 Sep 2026 (Everest; $2M milestone). EU MAA (TACHYMIST) decision is expected 1H 2027 (an earlier filing said Q1 2027). ReVeRA-301 AFib-RVR Phase 3 started Aug 2026. The labeled dose (70 mg) is from memory and was left off the card. RAPID/NODE-301 (NCT03464019) shows 'TERMINATED' on CT.gov, but it was the pivotal efficacy study. (2) XHANCE: deal closed on or before 22 May 2025 (shareholders approved 16 May). No 2026 sales or CVR news found. (3) LYR-220: no 2025-26 status found, so it is folded into the LYR-210 card as stopped. Treat that as UNVERIFIED. LYR-210 assets may still be sold; no transaction found. (4) SINUVA (Medtronic mometasone sinus implant): the product page is still live, use has fallen sharply since 2021 per FDA Sentinel, and no discontinuation notice was found. No card because there is no datable 2025-26 event. (5) NATESTO: Acerus is the marketer per DailyMed (Jul 2025 label). Aytu's status after the amended deal is UNVERIFIED. (6) WL1006: 'Shanghai World Leader' (CT.gov) and 'Shanghai Shiling' (Reuters) are probably the same company (世领 = 'world lead'), but this is an inference. (7) PG-011 = pumecitinib (CT.gov names it 'Pumecitinib Nasal Spray'). The JAK mechanism is inferred from the INN stem only. Its Phase 3 record has not been updated since Aug 2025. (8) ALDP001 and VVN432: API and mechanism unknown. (9) No intranasal biologic (e.g., nasal anti-IL-4R) for CRSwNP or AR was found; all such biologics are injected (dupilumab, stapokibart, etc.). (10) Skipped or not carded: Nascobal (2005 approval; DailyMed lists Par Health and QOL Medical as labelers); nasal calcitonin (old, status unchecked); Noctiva (discontinued, not re-verified because search budget ran out); nasal glucagon/Baqsimi (assumed to be in the Emergency agent's slice); intranasal insulin (all current trials are CNS/academic, e.g., NCT07675499 Rutgers T2D cognition); HHT topical tacrolimus/timolol/bevacizumab (academic and older); ED tranexamic-acid powder for epistaxis (NCT06997796, small academic study in Canada); ENA Respiratory INNA-051 (infection agent's slice). Korea: Ryaltris is approved in South Korea (partner not verified).
